A0013.title: Client Application Hardening
A0013.definition: Applying code-level obfuscation, anti-debugging, and other protections to front-end JS scripts or client APPs.
A0013.description: Client-side code obfuscation can, to some extent, prevent black-gray industry actors from directly reverse-engineering client-side code to analyze resource access logic and implement business automation and data scraping. It also increases the difficulty of breaking client-side human verification challenges, abnormal environment detection (A0010), API signatures (A0002), and other business security measures. However, because the obfuscated code still resides on the user's client, it is theoretically possible to fully reverse the obfuscated code given sufficient time and effort. Therefore, client-side code obfuscation is only a means of reducing the ROI of black-gray industry actors. However, according to the PDR formula Pt > Dt + Rt, if defenders can reduce the obfuscation cycle to within the cracking cycle, long-term protection may be achievable. Anti-debugging can be either a blocking mechanism against debugging or an interference mechanism — for example, one program logic can run in a non-debug environment and a different logic in a debug environment.
A0013.limitation: Hardened applications can still be decompiled: although hardening increases the difficulty of decompilation, it cannot completely prevent it. Hackers can use various means to crack hardened applications and obtain source code and sensitive information. Hardened applications may have compatibility issues: since hardening modifies the application's code and structure, it may cause compatibility problems — for example, the hardened application may not run on certain devices or may crash. Hardened applications may have performance issues: since hardening increases the application's size and runtime overhead, it may cause performance problems such as slower startup or higher memory usage.

A0013-001.title: Android Application Hardening
A0013-001.definition: Hardening Android applications through anti-reverse engineering, anti-tampering, anti-debugging, and anti-malware measures.
A0013-001.description: Multiple protection modes for DEX combined with VMP virtual machine encrypt and protect critical code and core logic, preventing source code extraction via reverse engineering tools such as IDA, JEB, JADX, APKTool, and Readelf. Each file in the App is assigned a unique identification fingerprint, combined with signature and file integrity checks; replacing any file will prevent execution, thereby blocking malicious cracking such as ad virus injection, repackaging, and feature disabling. Multiple encryption technologies combined with low-level countermeasures prevent code injection and block dynamic debugging at both the Java and native layers, effectively resisting dynamic debugging, memory dumping, code injection, hooking, and other malicious attacks. Effectively detects and counters ROOT, emulators, screen hijacking, multi-instance tools, Xposed plugins, Frida, and various hooking tools (source: dun.163.com).
A0013-001.limitation: Potential compatibility issues and runtime performance overhead may exist. The hardened APK can still be decompiled or dynamically debugged by reverse engineering and hooking tools such as IDA, JADX, Frida, and Xposed. Attackers may bypass ROOT detection and integrity checks using emulators, multi-instance environments, or device spoofing. Hardening only raises the bar for cracking rather than providing absolute prevention.

A0013-002.title: iOS Application Hardening
A0013-002.definition: Hardening iOS applications through anti-reverse engineering, anti-tampering, anti-debugging, and anti-malware measures.
A0013-002.description: Encrypts strings to prevent keyword-based location of core business logic via tools like IDA; applies multiple code obfuscation techniques to increase code complexity and reverse engineering difficulty without affecting original logic or performance; obfuscates application symbols to raise the bar for code reversal; employs advanced anti-debugging techniques to block dynamic analysis by attackers and malicious analysts; protects binary code to stop reverse engineering tools from decompiling it into pseudo-code; safeguards in-app numerical values (e.g., attack power, health points in games) against tampering by memory modifiers; enforces application integrity protection to prevent tampering, repackaging, and other cheating behaviors (source: dun.163.com).
A0013-002.limitation: May introduce compatibility issues and runtime performance overhead; on jailbroken devices, tools such as IDA, Frida, and Cycript can still decompile or dynamically debug the application, and attackers can bypass string encryption and integrity checks via hooking, memory dumping, and resigning/tampering, making it difficult for hardening to completely prevent reverse engineering in jailbroken environments.

A0013-003.title: H5/Mini-Program Hardening
A0013-003.definition: Hardening H5 applications through anti-reverse engineering, anti-tampering, anti-debugging, and anti-malware measures.
A0013-003.description: Strengthens H5 applications through anti-reverse engineering, anti-tampering, anti-debugging, and anti-malware measures. Uses encryption techniques to counter dynamic analysis, preventing code from being debugged and cracked and data from being extracted. Supports strong binding of H5 applications to specified domains to prevent domain tampering that could lead to user redirection or even fraud. Encrypts code and script files, including dynamic encryption and decryption of strings, function names, and expressions, and obfuscates variables to increase the difficulty of reverse engineering. Also supports code file compression to reduce application size. Protects data using encryption techniques to prevent sensitive data from being obtained through network packet capture analysis (source: dun.163.com).
A0013-003.limitation: May have compatibility issues and runtime performance problems. JS scripts are inherently executable on the client side; even after obfuscation, they can still be restored or dynamically debugged using browser developer tools, packet capture tools, and hooking frameworks. Attackers can bypass domain binding and encryption verification by using emulators or proxies to tamper with request bodies. Front-end hardening is difficult to completely prevent reverse engineering.

A0013-004.title: Desktop Application Hardening
A0013-004.definition: Hardening desktop applications through anti-reverse engineering, anti-tampering, anti-debugging, and anti-malware measures.
A0013-004.description: Protect the application through encryption to prevent decompilation; apply obfuscation to increase code complexity and reverse-engineering difficulty without affecting original logic or performance; obfuscate symbols to raise the bar for code reversing; employ advanced anti-debugging techniques to block dynamic analysis by attackers and malicious analysts; safeguard binary code to stop reverse-engineering tools from decompiling it into pseudo-code (Pseudo-Code); protect in-app numerical values to prevent tampering by memory editors, such as attack power or health values in games; enforce integrity protection to deter cracking, repackaging, and other cheating behaviors.
A0013-004.limitation: May introduce compatibility issues and runtime performance overhead; the hardened program can still be dynamically analyzed by disassemblers and debuggers such as IDA, x64dbg, OllyDbg, and Cheat Engine; attackers can bypass anti-debugging and integrity checks through hooking, memory modification, repackaging, and other tampering methods; hardening only raises the reverse-engineering barrier rather than providing absolute protection.
